calls.head: Expect Anaheim to fire from everywhere
calls.body: Anaheim ranks 9th of 32 for shot volume (59.8 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5); Winnipeg ranks 24th for shot suppression.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 4 games this season
calls.happened: Anaheim took 44.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against their usual 59.8.

calls.head: Two of the league’s busiest games meet
calls.body: Anaheim’s games average 86.1 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined (2nd of 32 for pace); Winnipeg’s average 83.8 (8th).
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 4 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 64.4 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the two teams’ usual 84.9 and a league average of 82.0.

WPG.head: We had this close to even (46% for Winnipeg), and it went Anaheim’s way.

ANA.head: We had this close to even (54% for Anaheim), and Anaheim came through.

surprises.head: Anaheim got the good looks
surprises.body: Anaheim’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: a 9.2% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (league average 6.4%). A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: Winnipeg hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Winnipeg’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 46, against their usual 89 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

story.head: The Ducks roll past the Jets
paras: Judd Caulfield opened the scoring late in the first. Five different Ducks scored.
The chances were closer than the score. By our Swing measure, Tim Washe had the best night of anyone.

items.text: The Jets’ three-game winning streak is over.
None of the preview’s two calls held.
